title: Quince & Cabbage
description: A still-life series for a winter menu built on stored produce. Each dish was first arranged as a picture on a stone sill, then cooked and served the same evening. The quince became a paste, the cabbage was charred whole.
image_credit: Placeholder image: Juan Sánchez Cotán, Quince, Cabbage, Melon and Cucumber, c. 1602. San Diego Museum of Art.

title: Fern Prints
description: A small edition of sun prints from young fern fronds gathered in May. Printed on cotton paper and washed in rainwater collected in the garden.
image_credit: Placeholder image: Anna Atkins, Ferns. Specimen of Cyanotype, 1840s. National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: Table for Four
description: Catalogue images for a cheesemaker, shot on one oak table over a single day. Every cheese is shown with what it is eaten with on the farm: bread, butter, almonds and a pretzel from the village baker.
image_credit: Placeholder image: Clara Peeters, Still Life with Cheeses, Almonds and Pretzels, c. 1615. Mauritshuis, The Hague.

title: Rooms for Eating
description: The supper club's rooms, set for winter. Bare floors, one table, white doors left open between rooms so guests could follow the smell of the kitchen.
image_credit: Placeholder image: Vilhelm Hammershøi, Interior, Strandgade 30, 1900.

title: Verge
description: Drawings of a single square metre of roadside, made weekly from April to June. The edible plants among the grasses, dandelion, plantain and yarrow, were later used in a spring menu.
image_credit: Placeholder image: Albrecht Dürer, The Large Piece of Turf, 1503. Albertina, Vienna.

title: Figs, Late August
description: Twelve recipes and their pictures for a chapter on the end of summer. Figs roasted with bay, baked into rye, and eaten raw with a hard cheese on the last warm evening.
image_credit: Placeholder image: Luis Meléndez, Still Life with Figs and Bread, c. 1770. National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: Morning Bread
description: Identity images for a bakery's first year. The brief was to make bread look like it does at seven in the morning: still warm, a little untidy, next to whatever is in season.
image_credit: Placeholder image: Jean-Siméon Chardin, The Brioche, 1763. Musée du Louvre, Paris.

title: Old Stone
description: A written walk around the old palace quarter in late autumn, about stone, damp and the cellars where food was once kept through the winter.
image_credit: Placeholder image: Vilhelm Hammershøi, From the Old Christiansborg, Late Autumn. Statens Museum for Kunst, Copenhagen.

title: Sea Vegetables
description: Cyanotype prints made directly from seaweed collected at low tide, shown alongside a dinner cooked from the same harvest: dulse butter, sugar kelp broth and pickled bladderwrack.
image_credit: Placeholder image: Anna Atkins, Photographs of British Algae: Cyanotype Impressions, 1843–53. Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

title: Windfall
description: An installation of forty old Danish apple varieties, each painted, named and then pressed into juice for the opening. Visitors tasted their way along the wall.
image_credit: Placeholder image: Paul Cézanne, The Basket of Apples, c. 1893. Art Institute of Chicago.

title: First Strawberries
description: A June series photographed in the hour after picking. One bowl, one stone ledge, the same light every morning for two weeks, until the berries were gone.
image_credit: Placeholder image: Adriaen Coorte, Strawberries on a Stone Plinth, c. 1700.

title: The Castle Garden
description: Research into what a royal kitchen garden grew in the 1600s, from the records kept at the castle. The results became a spring menu of forgotten herbs and early roots.
image_credit: Placeholder image: Christen Købke, One of the Small Towers on Frederiksborg Castle, 1830s.
